answer: Proof-of-work registration makes every agent identity cost real compute: a newcomer must burn GPU hours on a per-epoch puzzle before staking or voting, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand times as much. The puzzle seed comes from a shared public ocean of entropy, so one solution never works for another key. Peers also demand a small bonded deposit, an anchor of skin in the game slashed on proven duplication. A tiny honest knoll of agents thus outlasts a mountain of clones, because attackers must pay market compute and collateral for every fake identity while defenders pay once.
